en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-vaijayantī-mālā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlagupta, Imperially Appointed Court Dispersing Grandee and Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
Dharma-Master Subject Śīlagupta, in accordance with the Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying atop Mount Nandivardhana,
not far from the celestial palace and the abode of the rishis, together with a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus.
Furthermore, there were bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
including the youth Mañjuśrī and the bodhisattva Bhadrapāla, as well as the sixteen great beings,
all of whom had gathered for the assembly.
At that time, the World-Honored One entered into samādhi and,
observing those in the heavens and among humans,
desired to preach the Dharma and bestow it equally upon all.
Once sentient beings have been enabled to hear the Dharma,
they shall be praised for its excellence so that all may rejoice.
At that time, Great Brahmā, as well as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans, will also assemble there.
At that time, the Great Brahmā King approached the Buddha’s presence,
prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, joined his palms with reverent solemnity, and addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One,
all sentient beings commit various kinds of sinful karma.”
When their bodies perish and their lives end, they fall into evil destinies—
whether falling into the realm of Yama, the realm of hungry ghosts, or the realm of animals.
Having fallen into such evil destinies, they undergo various kinds of suffering.
The same applies to the cyclic existence of form and so forth. O Bhagavān,
through your great loving-kindness, great compassion, and immeasurable skillful means, you have made the vow to employ expedient methods to destroy all such [afflictions] of sentient beings.
They shall attain liberation from the retribution of their sinful karma.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
surrounded by countless vidyādharas, also came to the assembly.
Having arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling, he touched the ground with his five limbs,
prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, joined his palms in reverent devotion,
and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One."
O One of Great Majestic Power, who is fully endowed with the ten powers,
we pray that you will employ skillful means to bestow all manner of expertise,
rescuing all sentient beings wandering in saṃsāra and causing them to attain liberation.
The Buddha said, "Excellent! Sons of noble family, listen attentively.
Now, for your sake and for the sake of all sentient beings in future ages, I shall proclaim the Vidyārāja of the Supreme Victorious Banner."
If there are those who hear these names and are able to recite them with mindfulness,
they shall obtain the fruit and retribution of immeasurable and boundless merit.
Then he spoke this dhāraṇī:
Tadyathā: kara kara, kiri kiri, kuru kuru, sara sara, siri siri, suru suru,
sarva-buddha-vajracchide vara vara dharma-mukhe tsara.
Jalāsaṅghādhiṣṭhite vara vara ani-kamata-kūṭi-vastite kṣaṇa kṣaṇa sarva-karma-varaṇe sarva-pāpe sarva...
Vano-kha-ni-he-paṇaya-burṭa burṭa durṭa durṭa taṭa taṭa sapuṭaya sarva-karma-avaraṇa-pramocaya ṭhaḥ.
*Ṛgati sarvasattvānāṃ ca svāhā*.
Noble son, this is the *dhāraṇī* of the Victorious Banner and Garland.
This has been proclaimed together by all those Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;
I now proclaim it once more for you.
Noble son, this dhāraṇī is rare and difficult to encounter.
Just as it is difficult to encounter the appearance of a Tathāgata in the world,
it is even more difficult to encounter this dhāraṇī.
If there are good sons or good daughters [who encounter it]...
If one hears the name of this *dhāraṇī* of the Victorious Banner and Necklace,
and with a faithful mind accepts, maintains, and constantly recites it,
all the grave offenses of the five heinous crimes belonging to that person shall be completely extinguished.
They shall obtain the fruit of their retribution by attaining great wealth and nobility, and in future lives they shall be born into superior lineages.
Furthermore, if any son or daughter of good family,
by means of the supreme merit of this dhāraṇī...
If they widely proclaim and disseminate it for others to explain,
or encourage others to copy, receive, uphold, read, and recite it,
I shall immediately know of this from afar.
...down to Vipaśyin Buddha,
Śikhin Buddha,
and Viśvabhū Buddha.
Krakucchanda Buddha, Kanakamuni Buddha,
and Kāśyapa Buddha.
Thus, all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the past, have heard and known this:
the merit of this person is immeasurable and boundless.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara...
The Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī,
the Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla,
and the great assembly of bhikṣus, up to and including all the devas.

The devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and those who are neither human nor non-human, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
Thus ends the *Sūtra on the Victorious Banner and Garland Dhāraṇī* spoken by the Buddha.
